blocks.html: The purpose of this volume is to make it easier for the non-expert to use \(\ell\)-adic cohomology. I hope that it will often allow him to avoid recourse to the dense exposés of SGA 4 and SGA 5. It also contains some new results.

The first exposé, written by J.F. Boutot, surveys SGA 4. It gives the main results – with minimal generality, often insufficient for the applications – and an idea of their proof. For complete results, or detailed proofs, SGA 4 remains indispensable.

The “Report on the trace formula” contains a complete proof of the trace formula for the Frobenius endomorphism. The proof is the one given by Grothendieck in SGA 5, pruned of every unnecessary detail. This Report should allow the user to forget SGA 5, which one may regard as a series of digressions, some of them very interesting. Its existence will make it possible to publish SGA 5 as it stands in the near future. It is complemented by exposé “Applications of the trace formula to trigonometric sums”, which explains how the trace formula permits the study of trigonometric sums, and gives examples.

The audience addressed by the other exposés is more limited, and their style reflects this. Exposé “\(L\)-functions modulo \(\ell^n\) and modulo \(p\)” is a “modular” generalization of the Report, based on the study of symmetric powers in SGA 4 XVII 5.5. Exposé “The cohomology class associated with a cycle” defines this class in various contexts, and gives the compatibility between intersections and cup-products. In “Duality” are gathered some known results, for which a reference was lacking, and some compatibilities. Exposé “Finiteness theorems in \(\ell\)-adic cohomology” is new. It gives in particular, in cohomology without supports, finiteness theorems analogous to those known in cohomology with compact supports.
For more details on the exposés, I refer to their respective introductions.
Finally, I thank J.L. Verdier for allowing me to reproduce here his notes “Derived categories (State 0)”. They remain, I believe, very useful, and had become impossible to find.
In the internal references of this volume, the exposés are cited by an abbreviated title, indicated in [ ] in the table of contents.
